summary: Allocates a 96-byte mutex/synchronization object, initializes it with MutexSynchronizationObjectInit, then allocates a 12-byte linked-list node holding it and inserts the node at the tail of the list rooted at this. The insertion is gated on the enable flag at this+0x88. When the list is empty (head this+0x18 is null) the node becomes both head this+0x18 and first-reference this+0x20; otherwise it links after the current tail this+0x1C. The tail is advanced to the new node and the count at this+0x24 is incremented. The initialized 96-byte object is returned even when the 12-byte node allocation fails.

local_names.this: list owner: enable flag at +0x88, head at +0x18, tail at +0x1C, first-reference at +0x20, count at +0x24
local_names.v3: initialized 96-byte mutex/synchronization object, the function return value

operations.description: Returns 0 immediately when the enable flag at this+0x88 (this[34]) is zero
OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(96) allocates the 96-byte object; a null result returns 0
MutexSynchronizationObjectInit initializes the 96-byte object with (v2, this); a null result returns 0
OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(12) allocates the node; on success it is initialized to [0]=v3, [4]=0, [8]=0, otherwise the node pointer is nulled
If the head at this+0x18 (this[6]) is non-null, the old tail's next at this+0x1C+4 is set to the new node; otherwise the node becomes both head this+0x18 and first-reference this+0x20
The tail pointer this+0x1C (this[7]) is advanced to the new node
The node count at this+0x24 (this[9]) is incremented
Returns v3, the initialized 96-byte object, regardless of whether the node allocation succeeded

clean_pseudocode: if (this[6]) { *(void**)(this[7]+4) = v4; } else { this[6] = v4; this[8] = v4; }
